title: Decision Practice
subtitle: Stop & Decide prompts to build active clinical judgment
howToUse: These decision points interrupt passive reading and force active thinking. For each scenario, pause and write your response. Then compare with the model response. Focus on (1) the immediate risk, (2) the safest first nursing action, and (3) what data you must check next.

decisions.title: Acute chest pain (possible MI)
decisions.scenario:
A 58-year-old patient presents to the ward complaining of sudden-onset, crushing chest pain that radiates to the left arm. The patient appears pale and diaphoretic and reports nausea. Vital signs show a blood pressure of 92/60 mmHg, heart rate of 118 beats per minute, and oxygen saturation of 91% on room air.

Stop & Decide (write your answers before reading further)

What would you do FIRST?

Why is this the priority?

What will you check or do next?
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Apply oxygen if hypoxic and initiate emergency cardiac assessment.
decisions.modelWhy: Unstable circulation and oxygenation threaten life.
decisions.modelNext: Reassess vitals, obtain ECG, prepare IV access.

decisions.title: Heart failure respiratory distress
decisions.scenario: A patient with a known history of chronic heart failure is admitted with worsening shortness of breath. The patient is unable to lie flat, is using accessory muscles to breathe, and has audible crackles on auscultation. Oxygen saturation is 88% on room air.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)

decisions.title: Post‑op sudden dyspnea
decisions.scenario: One day after hip replacement surgery, a patient suddenly complains of sharp chest pain and difficulty breathing. The patient appears anxious, respiratory rate is increased, and heart rate is 124 beats per minute. The surgical site is intact and dry.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Apply oxygen and call rapid response.
